chapters.label: Why film and replay travel together

delivery.title: Ten Impossible Worlds, One Verifiable History

opening.headline: What changed - and can we trust it?
opening.narration: When a shared notebook changes, numbered history helps you see what happened without erasing earlier pages. Software needs something similar. State is the information a program currently holds. Frame Chains organizes that changing state as records that can be checked, linked, and replayed. A convincing screen is not enough: we need to know which change was allowed and which accepted state can still be trusted.
on_screen_text: Familiar anchor: a shared notebook with numbered history
State: the information a program currently holds
Frame Chains: linked, checkable records of changing software state
Why it matters: a convincing screen alone cannot establish an allowed change

opening.headline: A frame is a data record
opening.narration: A frame is one recorded event or state description, not a picture in a movie. A chain links those records into a checkable history. A hash is a fingerprint computed from data: it can reveal changed bytes, but cannot by itself prove a story or a cause. A verifier checks the recorded data and rules. The accepted head is the latest record that passed those checks.
on_screen_text: Frame: one data record, not a movie picture
Chain: an ordered history linked to earlier records
Hash: a data fingerprint, not proof that a story is true
Accepted head: latest record that passed

opening.headline: Watch the rule, not just the world
opening.narration: These ten worlds are proof models: deliberately simplified programs that test specific rules, not real colonies or conscious digital people. A branch is a separate continuation of history. A projection or lens is a different interface onto the same history. A live replay is a running application you can pause and operate. Watch a valid change succeed, a bad change get refused, and the accepted state remain intact.
on_screen_text: Proof models: fictional programs testing specific rules
Branch: a separate continuation of history
Projection: another view of the same history
Live replay: a running app you can pause and operate

closing.headline: An inspectable history
closing.narration: The common idea is not Mars or a passport. It is an inspectable history of software state. Check what the model accepted, why it refused a bad change, and what remained unchanged. Now try one live example and test that rule yourself.
on_screen_text: Why was a bad change refused?

opening_cards.title: What is Frame Chains?
opening_cards.sub: Like a document's version history, linked records make software changes inspectable.
opening_cards.note: State is stored information. A frame records it. A chain links records - not movie pictures.

opening_cards.title: A fingerprint is not the whole truth
opening_cards.sub: A hash helps detect changed data. A verifier also checks the rules a candidate must satisfy.
opening_cards.note: The accepted head means the latest record that passed the checks.

opening_cards.title: These worlds are teaching models
opening_cards.sub: Watch a valid action, an explicit refusal, and the accepted state remaining intact.
opening_cards.note: Pause any app to try its controls. The fictional setting is not the claim.

before_apps.title: Alternative histories
before_apps.sub: Mission control models separate possible branches.
before_apps.note: Watch a valid branch, then a wrong parent reference being refused.

before_apps.title: Software identity
before_apps.sub: The passport models recorded continuity across devices, not a human passport or consciousness.
before_apps.note: Watch a counterfeit fail without replacing the accepted record.

before_apps.title: Allowed repairs
before_apps.sub: The fictional colony has rules about which systems may be changed.
before_apps.note: A correct fingerprint cannot make an unauthorized repair acceptable.

before_apps.title: Different views, one history
before_apps.sub: Five interfaces read the same source.
before_apps.note: Find the inconsistent view without changing the underlying history.

before_apps.title: Evidence and causes
before_apps.sub: A believable clue is not enough to support every theory.
before_apps.note: Watch the model distinguish matching data from supported causal claims.

before_apps.title: Preserved disagreement
before_apps.sub: Different agents can report conflicting state.
before_apps.note: Look for both versions being retained rather than silently overwritten.

before_apps.title: Rules have history
before_apps.sub: A rule can be replaced by a later rule.
before_apps.note: Watch a decision based on a superseded rule being refused.

before_apps.title: Move the state, not a recording
before_apps.sub: The game demonstrates moving verifiable data between devices.
before_apps.note: Check inventory and provenance, not just whether the screen looks right.

before_apps.title: Test the boundaries
before_apps.sub: This is a laboratory for deliberately bad changes.
before_apps.note: Expect specific refusal reasons and a replayable record.

before_apps.title: Illustrated possible futures
before_apps.sub: The museum gives different branches a visual form.
before_apps.note: Watch a corrupted branch being isolated instead of erasing valid history.
